public_rationale: On August 16, 2022, Google described robots as largely industrial and coded for narrow tasks; this qualified account does not establish that no general household helper was for sale [e1]. The April 4, 2022 Stretch paper describes the RE1 as commercially available and reports testing with autonomous control and teleoperation [e2]. Amazon's September 28, 2021 announcement advertised Astro's following, reminder and home-patrol functions [e3]. These earlier accounts do not establish a purchasable robot with a demonstrated useful range of autonomous household chores on August 18, 2022, or establish that none existed [e1][e2][e3]. The claim remains unresolved on this evidence [e1][e2][e3].
limitations: The sources do not provide a comprehensive market record for August 18, 2022 [e1][e2][e3].

The Stretch and Astro accounts do not establish both purchase availability and delivered general household capabilities on the claim date; they also do not prove those capabilities were absent [e2][e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of August 2022, nobody can buy even a decently smart robot at any price.

statement.excerpt: Facebook M was canceled, and 7 years later nobody yet can buy a super-smart (or even decently smart) robot at any price.
statement.document_title: What’s wrong with Google’s new robot project

from_speaker: a super-smart (or even decently smart) robot
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes this a claim about a general-purpose household helper capable of performing a useful range of chores autonomously.
A research platform requiring substantial programming, a remotely operated machine, or a single-purpose appliance does not by itself meet that description.
The claim describes availability on the post date. Earlier product announcements provide context but do not establish the entire market on that date.
The Facebook M cancellation is outside the supplied normalized proposition.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous market evidence establishes that no purchasable robot offered the described general household capabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one robot was purchasable on the post date and demonstrated a useful range of autonomous household chores.

evidence.explanation: Stretch is a material candidate against a literal reading covering every intelligent robot. The paper distinguishes autonomous demonstrations from teleoperated chores and does not establish a ready-to-use general household helper on the post date.

evidence.excerpt: Astro can follow you from room to room
evidence.locator: Inventing a helpful, capable robot for your home; Brings Alexa to you around the home
evidence.explanation: Astro offered intelligent household functions, making an unrestricted reading of 'decently smart' questionable. This launch announcement does not establish the broader autonomous chore capability used in the contract.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contemporaneous market records and capability evaluations establishing that no qualifying general household helper was purchasable on August 18, 2022, or purchase records and capability testing establishing at least one robot available that day that autonomously performed a useful range of household chores.
